title: I’m making an isometric soulslike that runs in the browser on my own WebGPU engine
author: dpsmkr7
selftext:
**Chasm** is an isometric soulslike set in a dark fantasy world.

You start as a knight with a rusty sword at the mouth of a cave and fight your way down through the whole dungeon to the goblin chieftain’s throne room. Along the way you level up, loot chests and take better weapons from the fallen.

Once the dungeon is cleared, the open world begins.

The game runs on my own WebGPU engine: volumetric lighting, real-time cloth physics for capes and banners, ragdolls, and shader-based water and lava. It plays right in the browser, including on phones.

It’s still in development: one dungeon and the start of the open world are done.

Play: [https://chasm.layero.app/](https://chasm.layero.app/) 

(0.5 GB, All modern browsers except Firefox)

comments.author: 6-7-xDDDDDDDDD
comments.body: Genuinely asking why you would do this in a browser? Who plays soulslike games in the browser? Surely the audience isn't there?

replies.author: dpsmkr7
replies.body:
It's easy to develop for multiple platforms, and all you have to do to play is click a link. From what I've noticed, Claude is better at browser-based games, plus I didn't want to deal with game engines. Something like that 🤷🏻‍♂️

As for the game's audience, I share it with my friends and on Telegram and Reddit—that's more than enough for me :)

replies.author: Three_Tails_Studio
replies.body: Because developing a browser game is infinitely easier than working within Gadot, Unreal, Unity. Its cheap and easy. Thats it.
